summary: Defines requirements for a baseline policy for Time-Stamping Authorities (TSAs) that issue time-stamp tokens backed by public key certificates, with accuracy of one second or better. A TSA may define its own policy, but it must include or further constrain these requirements.

eli5.summary: A time-stamp is like a trusted clock that signs a note saying a paper existed at a certain moment. This lists the rules such a trusted clock service must follow so people can believe it.

questions: why do digital signatures need time-stamps
what are the security requirements for a tsa
subtitle: Security and operational rules for trusted services that sign digital timestamps

tldr.problem: Digital signatures prove someone signed something, but they do not prove when it was signed. A trusted time-stamp can prove that a signature was made while the signer's certificate was valid, which is crucial for long-term digital evidence.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 3628 defines baseline policy requirements for Time-Stamping Authorities (TSAs) that issue digitally signed time-stamps: rules for key management, clock synchronization with UTC to 1-second accuracy, and comprehensive security and operational controls.
tldr.outcome: Organizations running TSAs can follow these baseline requirements to provide trustworthy time-stamping services that meet regulatory requirements for qualified electronic signatures and long-term evidence.

today: RFC 3628 is an Informational document that defines baseline policy requirements for trusted time-stamping services. It remains normative guidance for organizations implementing Time-Stamping Authorities, particularly those seeking to meet European regulatory requirements for qualified electronic signatures. The RFC references both the Time-Stamp Protocol (RFC 3161) and standards for long-term electronic signatures.

sections.title: Time-Stamping for Proof
sections.content:
When someone signs a document digitally with a private key, a relying party can verify the signature using the signer's public key certificate. However, verification only proves the signature is valid; it does not prove when it was made.

A time-stamp token is a digitally signed assertion from a trusted third party (a Time-Stamping Authority or TSA) that says 'this document hash existed at this exact moment.' If the time-stamp was issued while the signer's certificate was still valid, it proves the signature was made during the certificate's validity period.

RFC 3628 defines baseline policy requirements for TSAs that issue time-stamps, ensuring they operate with sufficient security and accuracy to support qualified electronic signatures and long-term digital evidence, particularly under the European Directive on Electronic Signatures.
sections.eli5: A time-stamp from a trusted clock proves when something was signed. This document sets the rules that trusted clocks must follow.

sections.title: Key Concepts
sections.content:
A Time-Stamping Authority (TSA) is a certification service provider that issues time-stamp tokens. It operates one or more Time-Stamping Units (TSUs), each with its own cryptographic key for signing time-stamps. The TSA maintains overall responsibility even if it outsources functions to subcontractors.

A time-stamp policy states 'what must be adhered to'; a TSA practice statement explains 'how it is adhered to.' The baseline policy in RFC 3628 applies to TSAs issuing time-stamps with accuracy of one second or better, synchronized with Coordinated Universal Time (UTC).

A Subscriber is an entity (organization or individual) that obtains time-stamps from the TSA. A relying party is someone who trusts and uses those time-stamps as evidence.
sections.eli5: A TSA runs a trusted clock service. It has a policy (what the rules are) and a practice statement (how it actually does it). Customers request time-stamps and others trust them.

sections.title: Cryptographic Key Protection
sections.content:
TSA private signing keys are the heart of trust. RFC 3628 requires strict controls:

Key Generation: Keys must be generated in a physically secured environment by trusted personnel under dual control (at least two people must authorize it) within a cryptographic module meeting FIPS 140-1 level 3, CEN Workshop Agreement 14167-2, or EAL 4 assurance.

Private Key Protection: The TSU's private key must remain inside the cryptographic module and never be exported. Backups are deprecated as too risky. If a backup is made, it must be encrypted and stored securely, with access only under dual control.

Public Key Distribution: The TSU's public key is published in a certificate issued by a certification authority operating under equivalent security standards.

Key Lifecycle: The certificate's lifetime must not exceed the period that the algorithm and key length are considered fit for purpose. Old keys must be destroyed completely when their lifetime ends. The system must reject any attempt to issue new time-stamps with an expired key.
sections.eli5: The signing key is protected in a special box that only trusted people can access with a second person watching. It never leaves the box. Old keys are erased when they expire.

sections.title: Time-Stamp Token Generation
sections.content:
Each time-stamp token must include: an identifier for the applicable time-stamp policy, a unique token identifier, the time synchronized to UTC, a hash of the datum being stamped, the policy identifier, and identifiers for the TSA, TSU, and country (if applicable).

The time value must be traceable to at least one UTC(k) laboratory operated by a national metrology institute. The time in the token must be synchronized to UTC within the declared accuracy (1 second or better). If the TSU's clock is detected drifting outside the stated accuracy, time-stamps must not be issued.

Clock synchronization must be maintained through calibration and protection against tampering or electrical interference. Leap seconds (adjustments to UTC) must be handled during the last minute of the day they occur, with a record kept of the exact time of the adjustment.
sections.eli5: The time-stamp includes a policy identifier, a unique number, the exact time, and the document hash. The clock must stay accurate within one second and synchronized to international atomic time.

sections.title: TSA Security and Operations
sections.content:
RFC 3628 requires comprehensive organizational and operational controls:

Governance: The TSA must have a documented risk assessment, a formal practice statement, and a management body that approves and reviews the statement regularly.

Personnel: TSA staff must have expertise appropriate to their roles. Trusted roles (Security Officers, System Administrators, Operators, Auditors) must be formally appointed by management and are free from conflicts of interest. Personnel cannot be appointed to trusted roles if they have serious criminal convictions.

Physical Security: Critical facilities must have controlled access and protection against physical threats and environmental risks (fire, flooding, electrical interference).

Information Security: The TSA must maintain an inventory of assets, apply appropriate protection based on risk analysis, and document security controls and procedures.

Audit Trails: The TSA must maintain logs of time-stamping operations for at least one year after the TSU's certificate expires.
sections.eli5: The TSA must have a written policy, hire qualified staff in defined trusted roles, protect its buildings and systems, and keep records of everything it does.

sections.title: Disclosure to Users
sections.content:
The TSA must publish a disclosure statement to all subscribers and relying parties that specifies: contact information, the time-stamp policy OID, at least one hash algorithm supported, the expected lifetime of the signature, accuracy with respect to UTC, any usage limitations, subscriber and relying party obligations, how to verify time-stamps, how long audit logs are kept, applicable law and jurisdiction, liability limitations, complaint procedures, and whether the TSA has been independently assessed.

This information must be communicated through a durable, understandable medium and may be provided electronically.
sections.eli5: The TSA tells everyone: what we do, how accurate we are, what you must do to use or trust our stamps, and where to complain if something goes wrong.
